title: CV checklist
intro: These are the {n} things I look at on every CV that reaches me, in the order you build one. Tick a check only when the PDF you will send passes it.

items.check: Built in the CV Builder, from your order and design, in one font
example: Order from Choose your CV (or the CV Recommender), design from CV templates.
One font for the whole page: Arial, Calibri, Cambria, Georgia or Times New Roman.
Started from a filled-in example or The Nothing CV? Every line becomes yours, or goes.

items.check: One A4 page, with the font and margins never shrunk to fit it
example: Body text 10 to 10.5 pt, your name 16 to 18 pt, margins 1.5 to 2 cm.

Too long? Cut the weakest line, never the font or the margins: an old school activity first, then a second interest, then the least useful certificate. A line you can’t talk about goes anyway (check 17).
Half the page empty? Earn one more true line (The Nothing CV shows how). Never stretch the spacing.

items.check: File named “Your Name - Articleship CV - Domain.pdf”
example: ✅ One domain: Riya Sharma - Articleship CV - Audit.pdf
❌ resume final (2).pdf · CV_v3.pdf · Riya copy.pdf
✅ Two domains, two files: Riya Sharma - Articleship CV - Audit.pdf and Riya Sharma - Articleship CV - GST.pdf

items.check: Your name as on your ICAI record, a name-based email and a phone you answer
example: ✅ Riya Sharma · riya.sharma@email.com · 98XXXXXXXX
❌ CA Riya Sharma · rockstar.riya99@email.com
Keep it on ring, not silent: HR calls from unknown numbers.
No “CA” before your name until you are one.

items.check: LinkedIn hyperlinked, with a custom URL that opens
example: ✅ The word “LinkedIn”, linked to linkedin.com/in/firstname-lastname
❌ linkedin.com/in/firstname-lastname-4b7a91203 as plain text
In Word: select it, press Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on a Mac), paste your link.
Click it and your email in your PDF: both must open.

items.check: Your city only, not your address
example: ✅ Pune
✅ Pune (open to relocate to Mumbai)
❌ Flat 12, Green Park Society, Kothrud, Pune 4110XX

items.check: No photo, date of birth, parents’ names, a declaration or a signature
example: Also out: age, gender, religion, marital status, Aadhaar, your ICAI registration number, and a “Resume” or “CV” heading. Your name is the heading.
A firm that needs these asks on its own form; the space goes to proof.

items.check: A three-line objective naming your domain, never a generic one
example: ❌ To work in a reputed organisation where I can utilise my skills and grow with the organisation.

✅ CA Intermediate cleared ([Month Year], first attempt); ICITSS completed. Kept the family shop’s books in Tally Prime for a year. Seeking articleship in GST, to learn monthly returns and ITC matching.

items.check: Education newest first, nothing below Class X, one marks format per kind of row
example: Columns: Year · Qualification · Institute or board · Marks · Remarks.
ICAI levels as marks out of the maximum, CGPA as CGPA, school as a percentage, with the same decimals everywhere.
Year only is fine; show a month in one row and you show it in every row. Short names (“ICAI”) keep every row one line tall. Every other section goes newest first too.

items.check: A remark on every row, and only what a marksheet or certificate proves
example: ✅ CA Intermediate row: First attempt · 74 in Taxation
✅ Class XII row: 98 in Accountancy
✅ AIR 34: only an all-India rank ICAI gave you
✅ Exemption in [paper]: only if your marksheet shows one (an Inter group passed later). One sitting, or Foundation? Write the score.
✅ School rank 3 of 140: only with a certificate or letter
❌ A blank cell · “City rank 2” · “Topper” with nothing to prove it

items.check: Groups, attempts and results shown exactly as they are
example: Groups cleared in different sittings: one row each, with its own month, year and marks, so every row shows a month.
Both groups passed together, but not on the first try: one row, year only is fine; the attempts answer is in HR round and GD booklet – Day 4.
Result not out yet: “Result awaited”. Never a score before the result.
A gap: no CV line unless you did real work in it; keep one true sentence ready (Guidebook ch 3, q11).

also.label: HR round and GD booklet – Day 4

items.check: ICITSS in its own education row, with its true status
example: ✅ ICITSS (OC + ITT) · Completed [Month Year]
✅ Ongoing, completes [Month Year]
✅ Batch from [Month Year]
Not booked yet? Book a batch and write its date: ICITSS must be done before your articleship starts.
❌ “Completed” while it is pending. Firms check, and one false line makes them doubt every true one.

items.check: Every line: verb, what, how many, with what, what came of it
example: ❌ Responsible for my father’s shop accounts.
✅ Recorded 1,400 sales and purchase vouchers in Tally Prime for the family paint shop over 10 months; reconciled the bank every month and cleared ₹38,000 of unmatched entries before the GST filing.
Past tense, one or two lines, no “I” or “my”, no two bullets on the same verb.

items.check: “Assisted” for shared work; no verb above a trainee’s level
example: ✅ Assisted in checking 45 fixed-asset additions against invoices
❌ Led the statutory audit
Pick a verb one step too high and the interviewer walks you down.

items.check: Certificates and simulations in their own section, four outside certificates at most
example: Heading “Certifications and job simulations”; never Experience, Internship or “virtual intern”.
ICITSS stays in education, and the MSC Articleship Program line isn’t one of the four.

fix.label: Guidebook, chapter 3
fix.find: Where do job simulations and certificates go?

items.check: No client names: the industry and size instead
example: ✅ a ₹60 crore pharma distributor in Indore
❌ The client’s name, even a famous one
Same for anything you attach: a work sample, a screenshot, an Excel file.
You may name your family shop or the firm you interned with; add one line on what it is: “a 12-person CA firm in Indore, audit and tax”.

items.check: Every line, skill and hobby survives two questions
example: Read each line aloud, write the two questions it invites, answer both.
Excel: XLOOKUP, PivotTables → “Share your screen and make a PivotTable of this.” “XLOOKUP or VLOOKUP, and why?”
Tally Prime → “Pass a purchase entry with GST.” “How do you reconcile the bank in Tally?”
Family shop GST: matched 40 purchase invoices to GSTR-2B → “What is GSTR-2B?” “What did you do with a mismatch?”
▸ More questions
SAP → “Which module?” “Name one transaction you used.”
ICITSS completed → “What did you make in ITT?” “Which Excel tools did it use?”
CARO 2020 → “Which companies does it not apply to?” “Name two things it asks the auditor to report.”
PwC US Audit Job Simulation (Forage) → “What is a risk-control matrix?” “Which control did you test?”
Reading → “What did you read last?” “What was its main idea?”
Trekking → “Which trek, and how high?” “What went wrong?”
Captain, cricket team → “How did you pick the eleven?” “Tell me about a time you dropped someone.”
Volunteer teacher → “What did you teach?” “How did you know it worked?”
▸ Skills and interests that survive
❌ Skills: Advanced Excel, Taxation, Communication
✅ Excel (proficient): XLOOKUP, PivotTables, SUMIFS
❌ Interests: reading, music, travelling
✅ Reading business biographies. Last read: [title]
Keep an interest only if you still do it and can talk a minute on it.

replace.Family shop GST: matched 40 purchase inv: Statutory audit Work Simulation: flagged 3 cut-off errors → “What is cut-off?” “What would you do next with those errors?”

fix.label: Practise your interview with this CV

items.check: Bold only the key result; fonts, spacing and dates even
example: ✅ Reconciled **₹4.2 lakh** of vendor balances for 60 suppliers
❌ **Reconciled ₹4.2 lakh of vendor balances for 60 suppliers**
Bold a number or a result: never the verb, never a whole line or section. Text left-aligned, never justified. Full stops at the end of every bullet, or on none.
Dates on one tab stop at the right edge, in one format everywhere: never “03/25” in one row and “March” spelt out in the next.
▸ Six more fixes reviewers make
1. Uneven space under headings → Set one Space After for every heading (Word: Paragraph, then Spacing)
2. A table past the margin → Narrower columns or shorter words
3. Numbered achievements → Use bullets: numbers suggest a ranking you don’t mean
4. Headings in different sizes or cases (“EDUCATION”, then “Work done”) → One heading style for every block
5. A bullet ending in one word on its own line → Cut a few words, or add a useful one
6. Two kinds of bullet (• in one block, – in the next) → Pick • once and copy that bullet into every block

items.check: Saved as a real PDF: text that copies, no “[” left
example: Download the PDF from the CV Builder. From Word: Save As, then choose PDF. Never a photo or a scan.
Search it for “[”: no fill-in and no line of the example applicant left.
Copy one line into a notes app: if it pastes as text, in the right order, a firm’s portal can read it too.

items.check: Phone and printout: nothing cut off, nothing faded
example: Mail the PDF to yourself and open it from that mail on your phone. Small text is normal on a phone screen; a second page, a cut-off line or text over text is not.
Print it once: grey text, thin lines and coloured headings must still read in black and white. Read the printout from the bottom line up: slips show when you can’t follow the story.

items.check: Same story on your CV, LinkedIn, cover letter and spoken introduction: marks, dates, titles and numbers match
example: Two CVs for two domains? Only the objective, the order of your proof and the order of your skills change. Marks, dates and numbers stay the same.

items.check: Before you send: the five-second test, after reading five classmates’ CVs
example: Read five classmates’ CVs first: after that, your own mistakes jump out.
Then leave yours for a day and look at it for five seconds only. Your Inter result, your best proof and your domain should show in the top third. If not, move them up.

done.title: All 22 ticked? Your CV is ready
done.text: Run the CV Reviewer on your PDF first. Then send it for Personal CV review on WhatsApp (+91 72288 81182) with your target domain and the one question you want answered, and attach the PDF. Fix what comes back, then run this list once more.
